## Purpose

This SOP describes procedures for collecting representative
groundwater samples from monitoring wells using the low-flow (minimal
drawdown) purging and sampling method. Low-flow sampling minimizes
disturbance to the well and surrounding formation, reduces turbidity
artifacts, and yields samples that are more representative of in-situ
groundwater chemistry than traditional high-volume purge methods.

The procedures follow the U.S. EPA low-flow guidance (Puls and
Barcelona, 1996), EPA Region 9 groundwater sampling procedures, and
the Cal-EPA Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) guidance on
representative groundwater sampling.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Sampling of existing groundwater monitoring wells
  with an inside diameter of 2 inches (5 cm) or greater, screened
  intervals of 3 m (10 ft) or less, and a water level above the top
  of the screen
- **Does not apply to:** Well installation or development; direct-push
  (e.g., Geoprobe) sampling; spring or seep sampling; wells requiring
  high-volume purging for regulatory compliance; wells with water
  levels below the top of the screen (consult the PI for alternative
  procedures)
- **Location:** All EA Program groundwater monitoring sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead | Approve sampling plan and well selection                |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate logistics, maintain well access agreements   |
| Trained Personnel | Purge and sample wells per this SOP                     |
| New Students      | Complete training before participating in well sampling |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Heavy well caps and locks; lifting pumps and
  equipment; uneven terrain around well pads; potential for back
  strain when bending over flush-mount wells
- **Chemical:** Groundwater may contain volatile organic compounds
  (VOCs), metals, or other contaminants. Purge water may require
  containerization as hazardous waste. Preservative acids (HNO~3~,
  H~2~SO~4~, HCl) in pre-preserved bottles are corrosive.
- **Biological:** Standing water in well vaults may harbor mosquitoes
  or other vectors
- **Confined spaces:** Flush-mount well vaults may be classified as
  confined spaces. Do not enter vaults. Sample from the surface.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change between wells)
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Steel-toed boots or sturdy closed-toed footwear
- [ ] High-visibility vest (if near roads)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

If a spill of purge water or preservative acid occurs, contain with
absorbent materials and refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
For general field emergencies, refer to
[SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Peristaltic pump or bladder pump      | Low-flow capable (0.1--0.5 L/min); peristaltic for shallow wells, bladder for deeper wells |
| Dedicated or disposable polyethylene tubing | Sized to fit pump and well; new tubing for each well if not dedicated |
| Electronic water level indicator (e-tape) | For measuring depth to water           |
| Flow-through cell with multiparameter probe | For monitoring field parameters during purging (pH, temperature, specific conductance, dissolved oxygen, ORP, turbidity) |
| Calibration standards                 | pH 4, 7, 10; conductivity standard; DO zero and saturation |
| Graduated bucket or cylinder          | For measuring purge volume and flow rate |
| Stopwatch or timer                    | For timing purge intervals               |
| Pre-labeled sample bottles            | From analytical lab, with preservatives as required |
| Deionized water                       | For equipment blanks and rinsing         |
| Well keys                             | For locked well caps                     |

### Field Documentation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Well construction logs                | Casing depth, screen interval, diameter  |
| Groundwater purge log (Appendix A)    | For recording stabilization parameters   |
| Chain of custody (COC) forms          | Required for lab submission              |
| Field notebook                        | For observations and deviations          |
| Camera                                | Photo-document well condition            |
| GPS unit or smartphone                | For confirming well locations             |

### Waste Management

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| 5-gallon HDPE buckets or carboys      | For containing purge water               |
| Drum or tote (if large volumes)       | For sites with contaminated groundwater  |
| Absorbent pads                        | For spill containment                    |


## Estimated Time

| Task                                  | Time per Well                            |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Setup (unlock, measure water level, deploy pump) | 10--15 minutes           |
| Low-flow purging to parameter stabilization | 20--60 minutes (site-dependent) |
| Sample collection                     | 10--20 minutes                           |
| Decontamination and breakdown         | 10--15 minutes                           |
| Total                                 | 50--110 minutes per well                 |


## Procedure

### Pre-Sampling Preparation

1. Review well construction logs for each well to be sampled: casing
   material, diameter, total depth, screen interval, and previous
   water level data
2. Calculate the volume of standing water in the well casing above
   the screen using:

$$
V = \pi r^2 h
$$

where $r$ is the inside radius of the casing and $h$ is the height
of the water column above the bottom of the well (or above the top
of the screen, for estimating stagnant casing water)

3. Calibrate the multiparameter probe per the manufacturer's
   instructions. Record calibration data on the purge log.
4. Assemble pump, tubing, and flow-through cell. For non-dedicated
   equipment, decontaminate with deionized water before use at each
   well.

### Water Level Measurement

1. Remove the well cap. Note the condition of the well (damage,
   standing water in vault, obstructions).
2. Wipe the e-tape sensor with a clean paper towel
3. Lower the e-tape slowly into the well until the alarm sounds at
   the water surface
4. Record depth to water from the surveyed reference point (typically
   the top of casing, or TOC) to the nearest 0.3 cm (0.01 ft)
5. Measure well depth from the same reference point (measure after
   sampling, not before, to avoid resuspending settled solids)
6. Calculate the water column height and standing water volume

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Always measure water level before inserting the pump. Lowering the
pump displaces water and changes the apparent water level.
:::

### Pump Placement and Low-Flow Purging

1. Slowly lower the pump intake to the center of the screened interval
   (or the target sampling depth specified in the sampling plan).
   Avoid dropping the pump or allowing it to contact the bottom of
   the well.
2. Start the pump at the lowest speed setting and slowly increase
   until discharge begins. Target a flow rate of 0.1--0.5 L/min.
3. Check the water level. Drawdown should not exceed 10 cm (0.33 ft)
   during purging. If drawdown exceeds 10 cm, reduce the pumping
   rate.
4. Route the discharge through the flow-through cell for continuous
   monitoring of field parameters.
5. Record field parameters (pH, temperature, specific conductance,
   dissolved oxygen, ORP, turbidity) and cumulative purge volume on
   the purge log at 3--5 minute intervals.
6. Continue purging until field parameters have stabilized.
   Stabilization criteria:

| Parameter              | Stabilization Criterion               |
|:-----------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| pH                     | +/- 0.1 units over three consecutive readings |
| Temperature            | +/- 0.2 C over three consecutive readings     |
| Specific conductance   | +/- 3% over three consecutive readings        |
| Dissolved oxygen       | +/- 0.3 mg/L over three consecutive readings  |
| ORP                    | +/- 10 mV over three consecutive readings     |
| Turbidity              | +/- 10% over three consecutive readings (or < 10 NTU) |

7. Once all parameters are stable, proceed immediately to sample
   collection. Do not turn off the pump between purging and sampling.

::: {.callout-important}
### If the Well Purges Dry

If the well dewaters before stabilization is achieved, stop pumping
and allow the well to recover. Sample as soon as adequate volume has
recovered (ideally within 24 hours). Record the dewatering event and
recovery time on the purge log. Note that samples from wells purged
to dryness may not be representative.
:::

### Sample Collection

1. Disconnect the flow-through cell from the discharge line. Collect
   samples directly from the pump tubing.
2. Maintain the same low flow rate used during purging.
3. Collect samples in the following order to minimize bias from
   changes in flow or chemistry:

   a. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs), if applicable -- fill
      directly into 40 mL glass vials with zero headspace; do not
      filter
   b. Dissolved gases, if applicable
   c. Total metals and other unfiltered analytes
   d. Filtered (dissolved) analytes -- attach a 0.45 um in-line
      filter to the discharge tubing
   e. General chemistry (pH, conductivity, alkalinity, nutrients)
   f. Bacteria (use sterile bottles)

4. Fill bottles slowly to minimize aeration and turbulence. Tilt the
   bottle and let water flow down the inside wall.
5. For pre-preserved bottles, do not overfill (preservative will be
   diluted). Fill to the shoulder of the bottle.
6. Cap immediately, label with site ID, well ID, date, time, depth
   to water, and sampler initials.
7. Place in a cooler with ice immediately.

### Post-Sampling Procedures

1. Measure and record the final depth to water
2. Measure the total well depth (now that sampling is complete)
3. Remove the pump and tubing. Coil tubing carefully if it is
   dedicated equipment.
4. Replace the well cap and lock
5. Containerize all purge water. Dispose of according to the site
   waste management plan (non-contaminated purge water may be
   discharged on-site per the sampling plan; contaminated purge water
   must be drummed and disposed of properly).
6. Decontaminate non-dedicated equipment with a detergent wash
   followed by deionized water rinse. Collect an equipment blank from
   the final rinse.
7. Complete the chain of custody form

### Decontamination Between Wells

If using non-dedicated equipment:

1. Flush the pump and tubing with a minimum of 1 L of laboratory-
   grade detergent solution (Alconox or equivalent)
2. Flush with a minimum of 3 L of deionized water
3. Allow to air-dry or flush with additional deionized water
4. Change nitrile gloves between wells
5. Collect one equipment blank per sampling event to verify
   decontamination adequacy


## Sample Preservation and Holding Times

Follow the preservation requirements specified by your analytical
laboratory. Common groundwater analytes:

| Analyte              | Container          | Preservative           | Holding Time    |
|:---------------------|:-------------------|:-----------------------|:----------------|
| pH                   | Poly, 250 mL       | None; measure in field | 15 minutes      |
| Specific conductance | Poly, 250 mL       | Refrigerate 4 C        | 28 days         |
| Alkalinity           | Poly, 250 mL       | Refrigerate 4 C        | 14 days         |
| Nitrate + nitrite    | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 28 days      |
| Ammonia              | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 28 days      |
| Total phosphorus     | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 28 days      |
| Total metals         | Poly, 500 mL       | HNO~3~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 6 months        |
| Dissolved metals     | Poly, 500 mL       | Filter 0.45 um; HNO~3~ to pH < 2; 4 C | 6 months |
| VOCs                 | Glass, 40 mL (x3)  | HCl to pH < 2; 4 C    | 14 days         |
| General minerals     | Poly, 1 L          | Refrigerate 4 C        | 28 days         |


## Quality Control

### Field Blanks

One field blank per sampling event: fill a sample bottle with
deionized water at the well site, preserve and handle identically to
field samples, and submit to the laboratory.

### Equipment Blanks

One equipment blank per sampling event: collect the final deionized
water rinse from the decontaminated pump and tubing.

### Field Duplicates

Collect one field duplicate per 10 wells sampled (or at least one per
event). Duplicates are collected immediately after the primary sample
from the same well at the same flow rate.

### Trip Blanks (VOCs Only)

If sampling for VOCs, include one trip blank per cooler. The trip
blank is a set of 40 mL VOC vials filled with laboratory-grade water
at the lab and transported unopened with the field samples.


## Data Management

1. Enter purge log data, water levels, and sample IDs into the project
   database within 48 hours
2. Calculate the water table elevation for each well from the depth-
   to-water measurement and the surveyed TOC elevation
3. When laboratory results are received, merge with field data and
   apply QC flags per
   [SOP-L802 Quality Control](../lab_sops/SOP-L802-quality-control.qmd)
4. Archive original field data sheets (scan if paper)
5. Version-control all analysis scripts per
   [SOP-L801 RStudio and GitHub](../lab_sops/SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd)

## Training Record

Before sampling groundwater monitoring wells independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd),
   and [SOP-F300 Surface Water Sampling](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd)
   in full
2. Review well construction logs for the wells to be sampled
3. Demonstrate proper water level measurement technique
4. Observe a trained operator complete a full low-flow purge and
   sample collection at one well
5. Perform a supervised purge and sampling event with parameter
   stabilization achieved within the criteria in Section 7.3
6. Demonstrate proper decontamination and chain of custody procedures
7. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
